notes: Concise table-ready mechanical reference for Core Rulebook Force powers. Paraphrased for Destiny Chronicle.

Battle Strike.check: Use the Force; the result sets the bonus for your next attack made before the end of your next turn.
Battle Strike.effect: DC 15: +1 Force bonus on the attack roll and +1d6 damage if it hits. DC 20: +1 attack and +2d6 damage. DC 25: +1 attack and +3d6 damage.
Battle Strike.special: The bonus applies to one attack only.

Dark Rage.check: Use the Force against a fixed DC.
Dark Rage.effect: DC 15: +2 rage bonus on melee attack rolls until the end of your turn. DC 20: +4. DC 25: +6.
Dark Rage.special: While raging, you cannot use skills or tasks requiring patience or concentration. Spend a Force Point to extend the rage through the encounter. [Dark side]: using this power increases Dark Side Score by 1, and a Force Point cannot modify its activation check.

Farseeing.target: One creature you know or have met
Farseeing.check: Make a Use the Force check to gain a distant impression of the target; familiarity and distance affect the difficulty and the GM supplies the vision/information indicated by the result.
Farseeing.effect: Provides a brief sensory or emotional impression of events surrounding the target rather than precise remote surveillance.
Farseeing.special: The GM adjudicates what the vision reveals; Farseeing is primarily an information power, not a combat attack.

Force Disarm.target: One target within 12 squares and line of sight
Force Disarm.check: Use your Use the Force result in place of the attack roll for a disarm attempt.
Force Disarm.effect: On a successful disarm, either drop the item in the target's space or pull it into your free hand.
Force Disarm.special: Spend a Force Point before the attempt to damage the weapon on success; it takes damage equal to your Use the Force result. [Telekinetic].

Force Grip.target: One target within 12 squares and line of sight
Force Grip.check: DC 15 = 2d6 damage; DC 20 = 4d6; DC 25 = 6d6. Your check must also meet the target's Fortitude Defense for the full effect.
Force Grip.effect: If the check meets Fortitude Defense, deal the selected damage and the target may take only one swift action on its next turn. If it misses Fortitude, deal half damage; the target acts normally and the power cannot be maintained.
Force Grip.special: Large and larger targets add a size modifier to Fortitude for this power. Maintaining it costs a standard action and a new check each round; taking damage while maintaining requires a concentration-style Use the Force check (DC 15 + damage taken). Spend a Force Point for +2d6 damage. [Telekinetic].

Force Lightning.target: One target within 6 squares and line of sight
Force Lightning.check: Compare your Use the Force result with the target's Reflex Defense.
Force Lightning.effect: Success: 8d6 Force damage and target moves -1 step on the condition track. Failure: half damage and no condition-track movement.
Force Lightning.special: Spend a Force Point on a successful hit to move the target one additional step down the condition track. [Dark side]: using this power increases Dark Side Score by 1, and a Force Point cannot modify its activation check.

Force Slam.target: All targets in a 6-square cone within line of sight
Force Slam.check: Compare one Use the Force result with each target's Fortitude Defense.
Force Slam.effect: Against a target whose Fortitude you meet: 4d6 Force damage and knocked prone. Otherwise: half damage and not prone. This is an area effect.
Force Slam.special: Large and larger targets add a size modifier to Fortitude for this power. Spend a Force Point to add 2d6 damage to targets in the area. [Telekinetic].

Force Stun.target: One creature within 6 squares and line of sight
Force Stun.check: Compare Use the Force with the target's Fortitude Defense.
Force Stun.effect: If you meet Fortitude, move the target -1 step on the condition track, plus another -1 step for every 5 points by which the check exceeds Fortitude.
Force Stun.special: Large and larger targets add a size modifier to Fortitude. Spend a Force Point for one additional step down the condition track.

Force Thrust.target: One object or character within 12 squares and line of sight
Force Thrust.check: Your Use the Force check opposes the target's Strength check. The target adds BAB, size modifier, and +5 stability if exceptionally stable.
Force Thrust.effect: If you win, push the target 1 square plus 1 additional square per 5 points by which you win. If pushed into a larger object, it takes 1d6 damage.
Force Thrust.special: Spend a Force Point to impose -5 on the resisting Strength check; a target successfully slammed into a larger object also takes +2d6 damage. [Telekinetic].

Mind Trick.target: One Intelligence 3+ creature within 12 squares and line of sight
Mind Trick.check: Use the Force vs. the target's Will Defense.
Mind Trick.effect: On success choose one: create a brief distraction that permits Stealth; feint so your next attack ignores the target's Dex bonus to Reflex; make a non-suicidal suggestion seem reasonable; or cause fear and make a lower-level target flee at top speed for 1 minute (ending if wounded).
Mind Trick.special: Suggestion requires communication. Spend a Force Point when suggesting to improve the target's attitude by 1 step, plus another step per 5 points by which your check exceeds Will. [Mind-affecting].

Move Object.target: One target within 12 squares and line of sight
Move Object.check: DC 15 Medium/2d6; DC 20 Large/4d6; DC 25 Huge/6d6; DC 30 Gargantuan/8d6; DC 35 Colossal/10d6. An unwilling creature also requires the check to beat its Will Defense.
Move Object.effect: Move the target up to 6 squares. You may hurl/drop it onto another target if the same check beats that target's Reflex Defense; both targets take the damage for the size tier.
Move Object.special: May be maintained with a standard action and new check each round until you deal damage. Damage while maintaining requires DC 15 + damage taken to keep concentration. Flying/hovering targets may resist with a grapple check. Force Point: +1 size category and +2d6 damage (subject to maximums). [Telekinetic].

Negate Energy.target: One energy-damage attack made against you
Negate Energy.check: Compare Use the Force with the damage dealt by the triggering attack.
Negate Energy.effect: If the check equals or exceeds the damage, negate the attack and take no damage. Otherwise take the damage normally.
Negate Energy.special: You must be aware of the attack and not flat-footed. On success, spend a Force Point to regain hit points equal to the negated damage, up to your normal maximum.

Rebuke.target: One Force power directed at you
Rebuke.check: Compare your Use the Force result with the activating user's Use the Force result.
Rebuke.effect: Meet the opposing result: negate/redirect the power and suffer no effect. Exceed it by 5+: you may turn the power back on its creator, using the creator's original activation result for its effect.
Rebuke.special: A reflected power can itself be Rebuked. If it is reflected twice, both participants are affected unless you spend a Force Point as a reaction to avoid the effect.

Sever Force.target: One Force-sensitive creature within range and line of sight
Sever Force.check: Use the Force vs. the target's Will Defense.
Sever Force.effect: On success, disrupt the target's connection to the Force, preventing normal Force Point use and Force-power access for the power's duration as specified by the Core rules.
Sever Force.special: [Light side]. Treat this entry as a quick reference; use VIEW SOURCE for duration/edge-case adjudication until the full verified Sever Force text is incorporated.

Surge.check: Use the Force against fixed DCs.
Surge.effect: Until the start of your next turn: DC 10 gives +10 Force bonus to Jump and +2 squares speed; DC 15 gives +20 Jump and +4 speed; DC 20 gives +30 Jump and +6 speed.
Surge.special: Counts as a running start for Jump. Force Point: another +10 Jump and +2 squares speed. Destiny Point: +4 squares movement and all movement that round may be part of a jump without a Jump check.

Vital Transfer.check: Use the Force against fixed DCs.
Vital Transfer.effect: DC 15 heals target for 2 x target level; DC 20 heals 3 x target level; DC 25 heals 4 x target level. You take damage equal to half the amount healed, rounded down.
Vital Transfer.special: You may heal less than the maximum and cannot heal yourself. Force Point: take no damage from the transfer. Destiny Point: additionally move the target +5 steps on the condition track. [Light side].
